question: Since 2016, the Commission has entered into cooperation agreements in the field of migration with Türkiye, Tunisia and Egypt. These agreements raise serious concerns regarding the use of EU funds for regimes deemed undemocratic where serious violations of migrants’ rights have been widely documented.

We are very disappointed that these agreements do not provide for the involvement of and scrutiny by Parliament, or any fundamental rights impact assessments. Vice-President of the Commission Schinas1 recently made statements regarding a possible similar agreement with Lebanon and a visit by Commission President Von der Leyen has been announced2. We also understand similar talks may begin with Morocco.
In addition, the Commission proposed sending EUR 500 million to Jordan for macro-financial assistance, which we believe may be a first step towards a similar agreement. 1.
Can the Commission confirm that it plans to conclude a cooperation agreement with Lebanon and whether the visit in May aims to advance talks in that regard?
Will this agreement follow the model of similar previous agreements in terms of scope and funding?
What are the Commission’s plans regarding potential future agreements, including with Morocco and Jordan?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (8.8.2024) The pact on migration and asylum1 reflects a whole-of-government and whole-of-route approach to migration management, seeking to ensure coherence and effectiveness among the actions and measures taken by the EU and its Member States internally and externally.

The Commission works with Member States in a Team Europe approach to deepen comprehensive partnerships with third countries based on mutual interests and in respect of fundamental rights. The EU recognises the difficult situation Lebanon is experiencing domestically, further exacerbated by the regional tensions.
European leaders recently recalled the EU’s commitment to Lebanon’s stability and its strong support for Lebanon and the Lebanese people.

In this light, the EU has decided to strengthen its support to Lebanon by providing more predictability and reliability of the EU support in the context of the current crises and the overall stability of the country, through EUR 1 billion in grants to Lebanon for the period 2024-20272.

The package will aim to help improve the overall economic situation in the country, strengthening basic services such as education, social protection and health, as well as supporting the most vulnerable people in Lebanon, including refugees, internally displaced persons and host communities in need, as well as providing support to combat human trafficking and smuggling.

Other priority areas where cooperation will be strengthened include: a) good governance, b) support to the private sector, c) cooperation with the EU agencies, d) integrated border management – addressing smuggling and trafficking of human beings, e) security, including support to the Lebanese armed forces, f) scale up cooperation with the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees on a more structured approach to safe, voluntary and dignified returns.

The EU-Morocco partnership is based on the Association Agreement3, which entered into force in 2000, while the Association Council frames the EU-Morocco relationship. The last Association Council meeting took place on 27 June 2019 and adopted a joint declaration4 which gave new impetus to the strategic, multidimensional and privileged EU-Morocco relationship.

Relations between the EU and Jordan are based on the Association Agreement5, which entered into force in May 2002. The EU-Jordan partnership priorities adopted at the EU-Jordan Association Council in June 20226 guide the relationship until 2027. The latest EU-Jordan Association Council meeting took place on 15 July 2024.
